transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, is it okay if I just jump right in? 

I guess I'm here because... well, I've been really, really driven lately. Which is usually a great thing in my line of work, you know, being an IT manager. I just have a lot of enthusiasm right now. But I kind of can't seem to stop launching new projects. I've been drafting all these new work plans, setting up aggressive certification schedules, completely upgrading our home network, and... well, sending a lot of messages to old contacts to network. 

It's all positive stuff, really! But, um... I guess I might be overdoing it a little bit? It gets pretty intense, and I sort of blow past normal limits without realizing it. It actually gets to the point where my wife, or even my director at work, has to step in and tell me to hit the brakes. I really don't want to cause any stress for my wife or make a bad impression at work, so I figured I should come in. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here.

Can you describe how long this period of increased drive and enthusiasm has lasted? Has it been a distinct change from your usual behavior, and do you feel like it's something others around you might notice?

Um, let me think... I guess, well, I wouldn't really call it a bad change, just a very... productive one? But, um, these stretches where I'm just incredibly driven, feeling really confident about everything, and maybe... well, maybe not getting a whole lot of sleep... they've been part of my life for roughly a year and eight months now. Give or take. 

And yeah, others definitely notice it. Like I mentioned, my wife and my director. I really try to keep it manageable because I hate being a bother to anyone, or coming across like I'm too much, but they definitely pick up on the extra energy when I get into one of those zones. 

Is that... does that timeline make sense for what you usually see? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
During these periods of increased drive and enthusiasm, have you also experienced a noticeably elevated or irritable mood?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I guess, well... I do get this feeling some weeks where I'm just... almost electric, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable. And it feels really great, honestly, to have all that positive energy. 

But, um... I guess I should be completely honest with you, even though I really hate admitting this... sometimes I can get a little... short? Like, if there's a tiny delay with a project, or even if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm working on... I might snap at her. It just suddenly feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. 

I always feel terrible about it right after, because I really don't want to be a difficult person or upset her. I try so hard to keep a lid on it and be pleasant. Does that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Can you tell me if there have been times when your mood was consistently high, irritable, or overly confident, even when things around you weren’t particularly exciting or stressful?

Well, um... yeah, I suppose so. Even on just a regular Tuesday, with nothing really going on, I can get this... well, I guess you could call it an overly confident feeling. 

I really hate to admit this, because I don't want to sound arrogant. I respect my colleagues, I really do! But, um... sometimes, when my energy gets like that, I honestly start to believe that I'm the absolute *only* person who can see the whole IT architecture clearly. It's like all the pieces just make perfect sense to me, and to no one else. 

I get so convinced that if people would just stop questioning things and follow my plan exactly, I could save the company from a major failure. Like it all rests entirely on my shoulders to rescue our systems. 

I mean, I'm really just trying to be a good manager and look out for the company, you know? I want to be helpful. But saying it out loud now... I guess it probably sounds a bit extreme, or maybe a little conceited? I hope I don't come across as a narcissist or anything. I just get really wrapped up in wanting to fix everything. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Can you tell me if these periods of high energy and overconfidence tend to come and go, or do they feel like they are just a constant part of your life without clear beginning and end points?

Um, let me think about that. I guess... well, they definitely do come and go. It's not just one big blur. But, um... if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make me sound like I'm too difficult to manage—if I really look back over the past couple of years... those high-energy, really pressured phases? They've definitely taken up more time than the down periods, or even just the quiet, normal times in between. 

I try really hard to just push through and be productive during those phases so I'm still doing a good job, you know? But they do seem to happen pretty often. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of how things have been going.
During these high-energy and overconfident periods, have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual, or that you feel rested even with very little sleep?

Oh, um... yeah, actually. That's... that's a really good question. I guess I haven't really thought of it as a problem, because it feels so productive, but... 

Well, I don't want you to think I'm neglecting my health or anything, because I really do try to take care of myself. But during those times, there have definitely been runs where I'll only sleep... maybe three hours? I'll wake up wide awake, sharp as a tack, right at 3 or 4 a.m. 

And the thing is, I don't feel tired at all. It honestly just feels like I've been handed this amazing bonus time to get a head start on the day, you know? Like I can finally get through my backlog without any interruptions. I always try to use that time well for the company. 

But I guess... I mean, I know three hours isn't what they recommend for a healthy adult. Does that... is that the kind of sleep pattern you're looking for? I hope I'm not doing something terribly wrong by just rolling with it when it happens.

Can you tell me if there have been specific periods — lasting at least a few days in a row — where your mood was clearly different from your usual self, and where people around you might have said you were acting unusually high, overly confident, or irritable?

Well, um... yeah, there definitely have been times like that. I guess... I mean, I really try to be easygoing, especially at home, but... there are these weeks where I just feel, I don't know, almost electric? Like I'm completely unstoppable and I can handle anything. 

But then... and I feel terrible admitting this, because I really love my wife and I don't want to sound like a bad husband... but during those times, if there's even a tiny delay, or if she just asks a simple question about what I'm doing, I can... well, I can snap at her. It's awful. It just suddenly feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down on purpose, and I get so frustrated. 

I always apologize afterward, of course. I hate being irritable with the people I care about. I just get so keyed up. Does that... I mean, does that sound like the kind of mood change you're asking about? I hope that makes sense.

Can you tell me if there has been a time when you felt unusually high, overly confident, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it was clearly different from your usual mood and noticeable to others?

Um, yes, I think we just touched on that, actually... but just to make sure I'm answering you properly... yes, there are definitely stretches that last well over four days. Sometimes it's a whole week or more where I get that... that electric feeling. Like I said, I feel completely unstoppable, like I can just conquer the world. 

And, um, yes, it's definitely noticeable to others. Like I mentioned with my wife... I really do try to be a good husband, but during those stretches, if she just asks me a simple question, I can snap at her. It's like I suddenly feel like she's—or anyone, really—is just deliberately trying to slow me down. 

I know it's not fair to her, and I always try to make it right afterward. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Does that answer what you were asking about the four days?

Can you recall if there has ever been a time when you felt unusually high, excited, or irritable for at least a full week straight, where your mood was clearly different from usual and others may have noticed?

Um, yes, I... I think we're still talking about those same periods, right? I'm sorry if I wasn't clear enough before, I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. 

But yes, absolutely, those periods where I feel electric and unstoppable... they definitely can last a full week, sometimes even a little longer. It's a very distinct shift from how I normally am. I usually try to be very steady, you know, for my team at work and for my family. 

But during those weeks... yeah, like I was saying, that's when the irritability kicks in. I'll be flying high, feeling great, and then my wife will just ask a normal question, and I'll snap. It just feels so strongly like she's doing it on purpose to derail me, even though I know, logically, she isn't. 

I really do try to keep it under control, and I always feel awful about it. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to live with. Does that... does that cover the full week timeframe you were asking about? I can try to explain it differently if that wasn't quite right.
Can you confirm if there has ever been a time when your mood was elevated, excited, or irritable for at least a full week without letting up, and it was clearly different from your usual mood?

Yes, um... I feel like I might be repeating myself, and I'm really sorry if I'm not giving you the exact answer you're looking for... but yes, that's exactly what I meant about those weeks. It really does last a full week, sometimes more, without letting up. 

I just get into this mode where I feel, like I said, almost electric. Like I'm completely unstoppable. But then, you know, it's that irritability I mentioned. If my wife just asks a simple question, I can snap at her, because it just feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. 

I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, or like I'm a difficult person. I really try my best to be a good guy. Does that... does that finally answer what you were asking? I can try to clarify more if you need me to.
